paragraphs: Four independent fostering services list Hull as an area they cover, and they are shown above. Hull City Council also runs its own fostering service for the city's children. An agency assesses, approves and supports its own carers and looks after children the council asks it to place; with the council you foster Hull's own children directly.

The council's Corporate Parenting Strategy for 2025 to 2028 sets out how many children rely on it. On 30 September 2025 Hull was looking after 770 children, 27 of them unaccompanied children seeking asylum, and supporting 568 young people who had left care. The strategy gives a breakdown of where children live: 26% with the council's own foster carers in Hull, 25% with independent fostering agencies, 14% with family or friends as connected carers, and 9% in children's homes.

Young people in Hull's care contributed their own statement to the strategy. Among the things they asked for was more foster carers and more choice of homes, so that they can stay close to their friends, their schools and their communities. Improving the supply of homes for children is one of the strategy's priorities.

If you live in or near Hull, talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies above before you decide. Ask how long the assessment takes, what training you get in the first year, who you can ring out of hours, and what you would be paid for the kind of fostering you have in mind. The East Riding of Yorkshire page lists more services nearby.
